_meta.source_note: The same NIBE Sitevision app that produced alarms_s.json, on its other route: 'noah' is the S series and 'emmy' the F series. The answer is {"result": [{code, text, textLong, extraTextLong, fvp, bvp}]} -- two fields more than the S route. Fetched as the page rather than as JSON: the route answers with the whole HTML page and the payload embedded in it, so it was cut out of the markup and parsed. The Swedish strings below are NIBE's own, verbatim: only whitespace was normalised, plus the pilcrow (U+00B6) and no-break spaces the S file describes.
_meta.coverage: Every code NIBE publishes on the F route (F370, F470, F730, F750, F1145, F1155, F1245, F1255, F1345, F1355, the SMO 20/40 and VVM indoor units, and their accessories). It is the whole generation, not just the F750, so codes for accessories a given house does not have can never appear.
_meta.numbering_warning: F-series and S-series alarm numbers are NOT the same alarms. 301 code numbers appear in both files; exactly one of them (604) carries the same text in both, and only three of the 301 are even similar. Serving an S-series text for an F-series code produces a fluent Swedish sentence about the wrong fault, which is worse than no text at all. The table is chosen by generation, never by what happens to be loaded.
_meta.text_confidence: High. `sv` is NIBE's own short display text, fetched verbatim. Where NIBE lists two or more wordings for one code (different control boards) they are joined with ' / '. 12 codes have no short text at all; 4 of those have no long text either, so for them the app has nothing but the number.
_meta.severity_confidence: Derived, not published, and derived by machine rather than by a person -- which is one step further from NIBE than the S file. NIBE's endpoint carries no severity field, so each code was classified by a rule over NIBE's own Swedish text and long text: 'alarm' where it names larmdrift, hjalpdrift, a blocked function or calling the installer; 'info' where it says operation is unaffected, that the pump starts again when the weather changes, or that it will make a new start attempt shortly; otherwise 'warning'. That gives 193 alarm, 251 warning, 17 info; ten of those were then reclassified by hand -- see hand_reclassified -- leaving 196 alarm, 241 warning, 24 info. The rule was written by running it against the S-series input and comparing with the hand-reviewed alarms_s.json: it reproduces `sv` on 478 of 478 codes, `severity` on 467 of 478 and `action` on 467 of 478. So roughly one code in forty is expected to be classified differently from how a person would have classified it, and nobody has read these 461 codes the way somebody read the S ones.
_meta.action_note: `action` is the last sentence of NIBE's longer text that tells the owner to do something, quoted verbatim; a full stop is added where NIBE left one off, and nothing else is written by us. `extraTextLong` is preferred over `textLong` where NIBE ships both, because there `textLong` is the generic 'see the heat pump's manual' wording and `extraTextLong` is the product-specific one; 57 of the actions come from it. 300 of 461 codes have such a sentence; the other 161 are null, which means 'we do not know', not 'do nothing'.
not_verified: Nobody involved in this project has an F-series pump. Not one line of this file has been seen next to a real alarm on a real display.
The severity is not NIBE's -- see severity_confidence -- and unlike the S file it has had no human pass over it.
42 codes have no long text at NIBE and carry only the short one, so their severity rests on a handful of words.

48 codes carry only NIBE's generic long text -- "Det har larmet genererades fran varmepumpen. Prova forst att aterstalla larmet. Aterkommer larmet, se varmepumpens manual for mer information." -- which says nothing about how bad the fault is, so all 48 land on 'warning'. Among them were 220 Hogtryckslarm, 221 Lagtryckslarm and 222 Motorskyddslarm, which are not warnings in any ordinary sense; those three are now 'alarm' by hand (see hand_reclassified). The other 45 are still whatever the rule made of a sentence that says nothing about how bad the fault is. The S file has the same gap on 45 of its codes for the same reason; it is NIBE's text that is thin here, not the rule.

Six codes (50, 51, 52, 58, 183, 221) carry `fvp` and `bvp` fields as well: alternative long texts for exhaust-air and ground-source pumps. They were not used, because using the wrong one of the pair would describe a fault the pump in front of you cannot have, and this file covers both kinds of pump. For those six the text here is NIBE's common wording.

Which register carries the number was taken from the F-generation maps in yozik04/nibe, not measured on a pump: 45001 'Alarm' (s16, read-only, 'Indicates the alarm number of the most severe current alarm'). Note that 45001 is 'Activate forced control' and writable on every S-generation map -- the same address, a different register, opposite direction.

There is no F-series equivalent of the S series' 32196 'Class 1 alarm' flag in any map the `nibe` package ships, so the app's fallback for 'the pump flags an alarm it will not name' has nothing to read on an F pump.
45171 'Alarm Reset' (u8, writable, 'Reset alarm by setting value 1') exists on every F map and on no S map. This app never resets an alarm on any generation.
The ten hand-reclassified codes were classified from NIBE's Swedish text, not from watching a pump raise them. Nobody has seen an F750 report 183 while defrosting.

hand_reclassified.why: The machine rule described in severity_confidence reads NIBE's long text, and these ten codes have either no long text at all or only NIBE's generic 'this alarm came from the heat pump' wording. The rule then falls through to 'warning' for all of them, which is wrong in both directions: seven of them are the pump narrating normal operation and three are the faults that stop it. Reclassified by hand, by the same rule the S-series file was reviewed under -- the text says an operation is in progress or that the condition clears itself, so 'info'; the text names a fault that stops the compressor, so 'alarm' -- and listed here rather than silently applied, because these are the only codes in this file a person has looked at.
hand_reclassified.rule: A code whose text says an operation is under way and will finish by itself -- a defrost, a start-up, a preheat -- is 'info'. That is the S file's own rule ('info' where the text says operation is unaffected or that the alarm clears itself), and it is the rule code 183 in alarms_s.json was corrected under on 2026-09-07 for exactly this reason: it repeated at Pushover priority 2 until acknowledged for a fault that goes away on its own.

to_info.175: Uppstart av mjukstartskortet pagar -- the soft-start board starting, which is what it does every time the compressor starts
to_info.183: Avfrostning pagar -- a defrost. An exhaust-air F750 defrosts several times a day in the weather it is for, and at alarm_min_severity: warning every one of them was a push
to_info.233: Avfrostning pagar -- the same, on another circuit
to_info.270: Forvarm. av kpr pagar -- preheating the compressor before a start, on a cold pump
to_info.998: startar / Startar -- the pump saying it is starting

to_alarm.220: Hogtryckslarm. NIBE's long text here is the generic one, so the rule had nothing to read; a high-pressure trip stops the compressor and is exactly what somebody running alarm_min_severity: alarm wants to be woken by
to_alarm.221: Lagtryckslarm -- the same, on the low-pressure side, and usually a refrigerant or flow problem rather than a passing one
to_alarm.222: Motorskyddslarm. NIBE's own action text for this one is 'Valj hjalpdrift och kontakta din installator', which is the file's own definition of 'alarm'; the rule missed it because that sentence is in the action field and not in the long text it read

hand_reclassified.not_reclassified: The other 451 codes are as the rule left them. The expected disagreement of about one code in forty stands for all of them -- see severity_confidence and not_verified.
